api.title: Public API
api.intro: Every published brand is available as JSON under the CC BY 4.0 licence. No keys, no sign-up.
api.envelopeIntro: Every response is an object with the metadata and the payload in `data`:
api.versioningBody: The API is at {version}. Removing a field or changing its meaning means a new version; adding fields does not.
api.attributionBody: The data is CC BY 4.0: use it, including commercially, as long as you credit the source with a link to {site}.
api.schemaBody: A brand's JSON Schema is generated from the project's Zod schema, so it always follows the data. Cross-field rules that JSON Schema cannot express are still checked by the project validator.
api.notesSearch: `/search-index.json` is not part of the API: it is an internal detail of the search and may change without notice.
api.notesDrafts: Only published brands reach the API. Drafts stay in the repository.
api.notesPrivacy: No personal data and no exact coordinates: location is the municipality and, on maps, the municipality centroid.

about.title: About the project
about.intro: Feito em Portugal is an open list of brands that make their products in Portugal. It is run by volunteers, carries no advertising, and anyone may use the data.

criteria.title: Which brands are listed
criteria.body: A brand is listed when its own website says its products are made in Portugal. Being a Portuguese brand is not enough, and neither is having products designed here. A foreign brand qualifies when most of what it sells is made in Portugal. When only part is made here, the brand page says which part.

check.title: How we check
check.body: Before a brand goes live, we find the sentence on its website where it says it makes its products in Portugal, and keep that sentence, with the link, in the project's source notes. The production location appears only when the brand gives it, and never more precisely than the municipality.

badge.title: The verified badge
badge.body: The badge means someone on the project confirmed production by some means other than the brand's website: a visit, a certificate or contact with the manufacturer. No brand has it yet. It is free and cannot be bought.

contribute.title: How to help
contribute.body: You can suggest a brand, fix a brand page or ask for your own brand to be verified. It all goes through forms on GitHub, where the work stays in public view.

data.title: Data and licences
data.body: The brand data is under CC BY 4.0: you may use it, commercially too, as long as you credit the source. It is available through the public API and in the repository. District boundaries come from CAOP 2025 by the Direção-Geral do Território.

images.title: Logos and photos
images.body: Logos and photos belong to the brands and are not part of the open data: they are not under CC BY 4.0 and the API leaves them out. We only use the logo a brand shows on its own website and photos it offers to the press or sends us. Every image is stored on our own server, so opening a brand page sends no request to the brand's site. If you work for the brand and want an image changed or removed, tell us through the correction form.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: The site uses no cookies and does not track visitors. We publish no personal data: many makers work from home, so location always stops at the municipality.

badge.title: The verified badge
badge.intro: Every brand on the list says on its own website that it makes its products in Portugal. The badge goes one step further: it means someone on the project confirmed that production by other means.

meaning.title: What the badge means
meaning.body: A brand is listed on the strength of what its website says. A brand with the badge has been confirmed independently by a project maintainer. The badge says nothing about quality, price or a brand's practices: only that production in Portugal was confirmed.

evidence.title: What evidence we accept
evidence.body: A visit to the factory or workshop, a certificate or official registration, photos of production, or direct contact with the manufacturer. The brand page shows the date of the check. Documents with personal data are never published.

process.title: How to ask for it
process.body: The brand fills in the request form on GitHub and says how we can confirm production. A project maintainer reviews the request, arranges whatever else is needed and, once production is confirmed, awards the badge. It is free and cannot be bought.

revoke.title: When the badge is removed
revoke.body: If production moves abroad or the evidence no longer holds, the badge is removed. Anyone can tell us through the correction form.

badge.empty: No brand has the badge yet.
